target: For every n, independent real cap-one density inputs and every real symmetric A with at least three eigenvalues of modulus at least one, prove a universal essential density bound for X^TAX or give a valid counterexample.

results: Theorem D' third-volume marginal threshold h<3/4

partner_result_applied.application: For M=I_3-(2/3)11^T and A=[[0,M],[M,0]], exact cross rank 3 and Delta=1 give ||p||_infinity<=3e for every admissible product law; this N3(1/2) example has continuous density by the partner L1 characteristic-function proof.

new_claims.statement: For canonical squared 3-minor volume sampling of M with Z=e3(MM^T), if a row i and column j have marginals >=h>1/2, then Z_ij>=(2h-1)Z. Writing M=[[a,r^T],[c,N]], if a!=0 and S=N-cr^T/a then exactly Z_ij=a^2 e2(SS^T); if a=0 then exactly Z_ij=sum_{P,Q}[r_Q^T adj(N_PQ)c_P]^2.

At h=3/4 inside N3(tau), a nonzero heavy edge obeys e2(SS^T)>Z/[2tau(1+tau)]>=Z/(4tau); a zero heavy edge carries hub-cofactor squared mass >=Z/2. No local packet or two-robust-singular-value conclusion is asserted.

unresolved_implication: QFORM-N3-SCHUR-E2-OR-ZEROEDGE-HUB-SMOOTHING-v1: consume the exact aggregate a^2 e2(SS^T)>=Z/2 or zero-edge hub compound norm >=Z/2 by a product-space/averaged-frequency inequality while retaining arbitrary same-bank curvature and the global third spectral resource.
